items.title: CONSENT CALENDAR

Award Contract No. HH-1019, 2023 Storms Remaining Road Repairs, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Njirich & Sons, Inc., in the amount of $13,577,969, and with a contract duration of 365 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year), to perform repairs to roads, embankments, and drainage facilities for Hetch Hetchy Water and Power that were damaged due to recent adverse wet weather events. The Planning Department has determined that this Project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and the Commission will rely on the determination to make its decision on this action. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the CEQA pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code Section 31.04(h)

Approve an increase of $430,433 to the existing cost contingency for Contract No. WW-769R, Various Locations Sewer Inspection No. 3, with Pipe and Plant Solutions, Inc., for a revised cost limit of $5,533,470, with no change to the existing duration contingency, for additional manhole inspection and additional sewer cleaning work at existing contract locations

Award Contract No. WD-2780, 8-Inch Ductile Iron Water Main Replacement and Sewer Replacement on 21st St. from Eureka St. to Church St. and on Hill St. from Castro St. to Church St. and Various Side Streets, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Michael O’Shaughnessy Construction, Inc., in the amount of $6,301,257, and with a duration of 628 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and nine months), to install water mains and sewer lines in the Eureka Valley Neighborhood of San Francisco. The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and the Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the CEQA pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code Section 31.04(h)

Approve an increase of $2,800,000 to the existing cost contingency and an increase of 270 calendar days (approximately nine months) to the existing duration contingency for Contract No. WD-2878B, Regional Groundwater Storage and Recovery Phase 2B, with JMB Construction, Inc., for a revised cost limit of $9,926,625 and a revised duration limit of 1,260 consecutive calendar days (approximately three years and five months), to address potential cost and schedule delays resulting from complications with procuring grid access from Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) for the site and to add scope for treatment facilities to remove ammonia that was recently detected in the groundwater at the separate South Spruce Avenue Well and Treatment Facility site in South San Francisco

Award Contract No. WW-766, Oceanside Water Pollution Control Plant 930 Administration and Lab Structure Health and Safety Improvements, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Blocka Construction, Inc., in the amount of $3,387,000 and with a duration of 790 consecutive calendar days (approximately two year and two months), to improve health and safety conditions related to 930 Administration and Lab Structure in the Oceanside Water Pollution Control Plant. President Arce left the dais at 2:24 P.M. to attend the Board of Supervisors meeting located within City Hall for a Board agenda item expected to be called at 2:30 P.M. Vice President Leveroni presided over the Commission meeting
Public hearing to consider the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan
items.text: Public hearing to consider and possible action to adopt the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan prepared by the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission for the City and County of San Francisco pursuant to California Water Code Sections 10610-10657, incorporating the 2025 Water Shortage Contingency Plan an affordable-housing development water service priority policy; and direct the General Manager to submit the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan and all incorporated documents to the California Department of Water Resources by July 1, 2026, as required by law. The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and the Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the CEQA pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code Section 31.04(h)

items.title: Award Contract Nos. PRO.0333.A-E, As-Needed Environmental Review Services, each for an amount not-to-exceed $15,000,000, and with a duration of seven years
items.text: Award Contract Nos. PRO.0333.A-E, As-Needed Environmental Review Services, to Environmental Science Associates, Inc. (PRO.0333.A); AECOM Technical Services, Inc. PRO.0333.B); Panorama Environmental, Inc. (PRO.0333.C); GEI Consultants, Inc. (PRO.0333.D); and Stantec Consulting Services, Inc. (PRO.0333.E), each for an amount not-to-exceed $15,000,000, and with a duration of seven years, to provide as-needed environmental consultant services under the California Environmental Quality Act and the National Environmental Policy Act and obtain resource agency permits, subject to the Board of Supervisors approval pursuant to Charter Section 9.118. Steve Robinson, Assistant General Manager – Infrastructure, congratulated GM Herrera on his retirement and introduced Karen Frye, Manager - Environmental Management Group, who also planned to retire at the end of the fiscal year with 19 years of public service

items.title: Approve an increase of 275 calendar days to the existing duration contingency for Contract No. DB-132, New Treasure Island Wastewater Treatment Plant, with PCL Construction, Inc.
items.text: Approve an increase of 275 calendar days to the existing duration contingency for Contract No. DB-132, New Treasure Island Wastewater Treatment Plant, with PCL Construction, Inc., for a revised duration limit of 1,479 consecutive calendar days (approximately four years), with no change to the contract amount, to allow for the delayed completion of the New Treasure Island Wastewater Treatment Plant, primarily due to increased equipment procurement durations, coordination issues with the distributed control system and program interface, re-sequencing required for tie-ins, ongoing coordination challenges with several external underground utility connections, and startup and commission work

items.text: Approve the Urban Watershed Stewardship Grant Program Requirements and Terms; and authorize the General Manager of the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission to negotiate, award, and execute grant agreements of up to $250,000 each
